node-4.label: Patient is a 94-year-old man with medical history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aspiration pneumonia, reflux esophagitis, dysphagia requiring nasogastric tube feeding, sequelae of cerebral infarction with left hemiplegia, mild hypoproteinemia and anemia, prostate operation with ongoing catheterization, and left eye blindness due to trauma

why.why: Expert laboratory analysis states that positive fecal PCR for C. difficile, post-antibiotic onset, bloody mucoid diarrhea, immunosuppression, and colonoscopic erythema from ascending colon to rectum collectively support active antibiotic-associated C. difficile colitis. Low CRP, normal albumin, and normal ileocecal valve further argue against IBD. The only remaining limitation is that toxin A/B or GDH testing was not obtained, so PCR positivity alone cannot fully exclude colonization; confidence is increased from 0.85 to 0.88.

The expert analysis reinforces that the positive C. difficile PCR, dysentery-like presentation, and colonoscopic erythema from ascending colon to rectum favor active C. difficile colitis rather than post-antibiotic gut dysbiosis. Low CRP, normal albumin, and normal ileocecal valve provide no support for dysbiosis, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.

Expert analysis states that low CRP, normal albumin, and normal ileocecal valve argue against severe or IBD-related disease, directly reducing the likelihood of IBD or CLL-related colitis. The positive C. difficile PCR and colonoscopic erythema from ascending colon to rectum are more consistent with C. difficile infection, so confidence is lowered from 0.10 to 0.04.
